muc.title: How does AI hear you?
muc.text: AI doesn't just read text anymore. It can also hear you talk. You speak into your phone, and the words appear right away. But how does a machine listen?

muc.title: What is a voice to a machine?
muc.text: To a machine, a voice is just a list of numbers: how the air vibrates, measured tens of thousands of times per second. Looking at those numbers, it's hard to tell what you said.

muc.title: Turning sound into a picture
muc.text: So the machine slices the sound very thin and splits each slice into low and high sounds. Line the slices up, and you get a picture called a spectrogram: bright spots are where there's sound.

muc.title: Reading the picture into words
muc.text: Each sound has its own shape: an "ah" is a few horizontal bars, a "sss" is a blur up high. A model that has heard hundreds of thousands of hours of recordings reads those shapes into words, using the meaning of the sentence too.

muc.title: Noise and people talking over each other
muc.text: Anything that smudges the picture makes AI mishear. Coffee shop noise blurs the shapes of words. When two people talk at once, their shapes pile on top of each other.

muc.title: Names are easy to get wrong
muc.text: AI rarely sees unusual names, so it often guesses a common word instead. A coworker named Leigh might turn into "lay". So always double-check names and numbers.

muc.title: Transcribe a meeting
muc.text: At your next meeting, ask permission, then record it with your phone close to the speaker. Afterwards, ask AI to transcribe it and sum up the 5 main points and the to-dos.

muc.title: It can listen. Can it talk?
muc.text: AI can listen now. What about talking? How does a machine read text in a voice that sounds human? See you in part 2.
